items.title: universal-lock: dependency without wheels for a matrix environment fails the whole resolution (marked per-dependency override works but undocumented)
items.reason: Exact duplicate: identical title, body, reported uv versions, workspace, error, marked overrides, and requested capabilities. Opened 17 seconds before this issue; neither thread has comments.

items.title: fix(pm): a plugin workspace stops resolving the Android split on desktop hosts
items.reason: Same hermes-agent/mnemosyne workspace and uv 0.13.5. Supplies a full onnxruntime failure in an Android resolver split and proposes excluding Android from generated desktop workspaces. Closed without merging. Strong application-side context, but it does not establish the cause of the reported sqlite-vec failure.

items.title: Add platform dependence to `exclude-dependencies`
items.reason: Maintainer explicitly explains that a marked override can omit a transitive dependency on an excluded platform. Directly supports the reported workaround; the original example concerns GDAL supplied outside uv, rather than missing wheels during universal locking.

items.title: Tracking issue: package without source distribution gets an "incomplete" resolution
items.reason: Canonical broader discussion of inferring platform coverage from available wheels and forking/backtracking accordingly. Its symptom is successful locking followed by installation failure, unlike this report's lock-time failure; it is related to the requested automatic availability handling.

items.title: Fork when wheels are missing platform support
items.reason: Attempted general wheel-platform-based forking for astral-sh/uv#9711. Closed without merging in favor of astral-sh/uv#10046, whose merged implementation only falls back from local versions to their base versions. Neither implements silently omitting unavailable dependencies.

related.search_scope: Searched astral-sh/uv open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged PRs with authenticated gh. Separate literal searches covered sqlite-vec, onnxruntime, compatible wheels, python_full_version, and override-dependencies; conceptual searches covered universal wheel availability, optional/best-effort resolution, automatic markers, and platform-specific overrides/documentation. Inspected candidate comments and followed references to closed proposals, merged fixes, and NousResearch/hermes-agent#144162. PR keyword searches returned no results; several REST searches were rate-limited, so GraphQL searches and direct linked-PR inspection supplemented them. Reviewed astral-sh/uv#21672, astral-sh/uv#10046, and astral-sh/uv#9827 for historical fixes. Ruled out astral-sh/uv#22805 as an established duplicate: it rejected existing Android wheels and was fixed by astral-sh/uv#22806 in uv 0.13.5; this report alleges absent wheels and supplies no complete failing split. Also ruled out astral-sh/uv#5921, which concerns metadata-fetch preference, and astral-sh/uv#8492, whose Python-version selection issue was fixed by astral-sh/uv#9827.

type_reason: astral-sh/uv#23037 already contains the identical report and both requested capabilities, so discussion can be centralized there. This classification does not assume the proposed missing-wheel mechanism is correct. No regression of a historical fix is established; the same current report already has an open issue.
summary: Exact duplicate of astral-sh/uv#23037. Related discussions explain marked overrides and wheel-based platform forking; an application-side PR documents a closely matching workspace failure.
draft_response:
This duplicates astral-sh/uv#23037; please continue there so we can keep the investigation together.

Marked `override-dependencies` can restrict transitive dependencies to selected platforms, as explained in astral-sh/uv#17642. The dependency-overrides documentation also describes marker replacement. To investigate the lock failure, please add a minimal workspace configuration and the complete resolver error, including the failing split, to astral-sh/uv#23037. The excerpt alone does not establish which platform lacks coverage.
